title: Research on Metro Transportation Flow Prediction Based on the STL-GRU Combined Model
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electronics and Green Energy (ICPEGE)
authors: Zijie Zhou; Huichen Ma
abstract: In the metro intelligent transportation system, accurate transfer passenger flow prediction is a key link in optimizing operation plans and improving transportation efficiency. To further improve the theory of metro internal transfer passenger flow prediction and provide more reliable support for intelligent operation decisions, this paper innovatively proposes a metro transfer passenger flow prediction model that integrates the Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) method and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU).In practical application, the model first relies on the deep learning library Keras to complete the construction and training of the GRU model, laying the foundation for subsequent prediction; then preprocesses the original metro card swiping data, uses the graph-based depth-first search algorithm to identify passengers' travel paths, and further constructs the transfer passenger flow time series; subsequently adopts the STL time series decomposition algorithm to decompose the constructed transfer passenger flow time series into trend component, periodic component and residual component, and uses the 3σ principle to eliminate and fill the outliers in the residual component, and finally completes the transfer passenger flow prediction. Taking the transfer passenger flow data of a certain metro station as the research sample, the validity of the model is verified. The results show that compared with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and the combined model of STL time series decomposition method and Long Short-Term Memory (STL-LSTM), the STL-GRU combined prediction model significantly improves the prediction accuracy of transfer passenger flow on weekdays (excluding Fridays), Fridays and rest days, with the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of the prediction results reduced by at least 2.3, 1.36 and 6.42 percentage points respectively.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Study on the Synergistic Optimization of Supply Chain Management and Financial Supply Chains from an Economic Perspective
authors: Han Wang; Huijie Tang; Ningai Leng; Zhoufan Yu
abstract: Based on economic theories and integrated with machine learning technology, this study explores a collaborative Supply Chain Management and Financial Supply Chain Management (SCM - FSCM) model to solve issues like efficiency loss, financing constraints, and risk transmission. We combine Transaction Cost and Information Asymmetry theories and use algorithms such as random forests to process multi-dimensional data and build a data-driven, three-dimensional (cost-efficiency-risk) analysis framework. We then apply an FSCM model of"core enterprise credit empowerment plus dynamic pledge financing."We use Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for demand forecasting and clustering/regression algorithms for benefit allocation. The study also combines Game Theory and reinforcement learning to optimize the inventory-procurement mechanism and uses eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for credit assessment to enable rapid monetization of inventory. Verified with 20 core and 100 supporting enterprises, the results show a 30\% increase in inventory turnover, an 18\%-22\% decrease in SME financing costs, a stable order fulfillment rate above 95\%, and excellent model performance (demand forecasting error<= 8\%, credit assessment accuracy>= 90\%). This SCM-FSCM model effectively reduces operating costs, alleviates financing constraints, and supports high-quality supply chain development.

title: A Framework for Enhancing Human-Computer Interaction of Cross-Cultural Language Large Models with Meta-Interaction Steps and CLeIDS Dataset
venue: International Conferences on Computers, Information Processing and Advanced Education
authors: Meiqi Zhang
abstract: This paper focuses on the challenges faced by large language models (LLMs) in human-computer interaction within cross-cultural language education, such as hallucinations in cultural expressions and insufficient handling of multi-step interactions. To address these issues, the paper proposes the AutoInteract framework, which decomposes complex teaching tasks into meta-interaction step sequences through the Cross-cultural Teaching task Planning (CTP) model and executes them using the Culturally-adaptive Progressive Prompting (CAPP) model, enhancing the handling of complex teaching processes. Additionally, the Cross-cultural Language Education Interaction Design & Steps dataset (CLeIDS) is constructed, containing 1,200 complex teaching tasks, 9,872 meta-interaction steps, and 32 tool interfaces, filling the gap in dedicated evaluation data. Experiments comparing AutoInteract with ReAct and TPTU methods on different model scales show that AutoInteract outperforms in all indicators, with its Task Success Rate (TSR) exceeding other methods by about 47% at the 69B scale, verifying its effectiveness. The model scale is found to positively correlate with performance, as larger models have stronger reasoning abilities.

title: A Fusion Prediction Model for Financial Market Volatility Based on Self-Attention Mechanism Convolutional Network
venue: International Conferences on Computers, Information Processing and Advanced Education
authors: Z. Liu
abstract: Traditional data fusion algorithms are less effective in integrating financial time series data under the same time dimension for financial market volatility prediction. To address this, this paper proposes a Fusion Prediction Model for Financial Market Volatility Based on Self-Attention Mechanism Convolutional Network (DAECNN attention) by introducing a denoising autoencoder (DAE) and a self-attention mechanism on the basis of Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN). The DAE is used to denoise and reconstruct financial time series data, and the self-attention mechanism is employed to enhance the extraction of key information affecting volatility. Experimental tests were conducted on AReM2016 financial dataset and HAR Dataset financial dataset, comparing with DCNN and BPNN models. The results show that DAECNN attention outperforms the other two models in fusion prediction accuracy indicators (ACC, P, R, F1) on both datasets, especially achieving 99.52%, 99.53%, 99.52% and 99.52% respectively on the AReM2016 financial dataset, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed model in financial market volatility prediction.
